name: Malaysia
sources: CPI inflation 2.62% and lending interest rate 8.79% (World Bank, 1990).

Federal government debt near 80% of GDP. This is high for the income level and it is real: Malaysia borrowed heavily for the heavy-industry programme in the early 1980s, peaked above 100% in 1986, and was still working it down in 1990. Most of it was ringgit debt held domestically, much of it by the Employees Provident Fund.
Oil 0.62 mbd: Petronas output from Terengganu and offshore Sarawak and Sabah, roughly 620,000 barrels a day in 1990, plus the LNG trains at Bintulu that do not appear in this field.

authoritarianism 0.45: elections are real and are lost in individual states, but the Internal Security Act allows detention without trial and was used in Operation Lalang in 1987, and the 1988 judicial crisis removed the Lord President. Competitive but not free.
separatism 0.09 is the Borneo states — Sabah under Parti Bersatu Sabah, which left the Barisan Nasional in 1990 — plus the twenty-point autonomy terms of the 1963 federation.
Military index 5: roughly 130,000 under arms, configured for internal security and the South China Sea claim rather than for any campaign.
Gross capital formation 32.4% of GDP (World Bank, 1990), entered as 11 state and 21 private.

Series check, August 2026, read from the World Bank API: NY.GDP.MKTP.CD 1990 = 44,024,585,240; SP.POP.TOTL = 17,833,171; FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG = 2.618; FR.INR.LEND = 8.786; MS.MIL.XPND.GD.ZS = 2.555; NE.GDI.TOTL.ZS = 32.360. All match. Federal debt near 80% of GDP and oil at 0.62 mbd are not on those series and are not verified to a primary source here.

pop_growth_1990 = 3.2460%/yr. Compound annual growth of World Bank SP.POP.TOTL, series MYS (Malaysia): 14,759,009 in 1984 to 17,314,997 in 1989 — the five years ending on the eve of the 1 January 1990 start date. See EconomyRecord::pop_growth_1990 in spheres-sim/src/data/mod.rs for why the window ends in 1989 and not with the single-year 1990 rate.

note: 1990 TECHNOLOGY: AUTHORED, NOT DERIVED. What this nation knew on 1 January 1990 is transcribed and sourced grant by grant, exactly like every other 1990 figure in this file, and is not read off tfp_trend - there was never a code path from the trend to the known set, and the zero that stood there was a claim about the world rather than an absence of one (BIBLE section 8 and iron rule 4, both amended 2026-08-30). THE PREDICATE IS SPLIT, and split by the technology's OWN EFFECT TYPE so that it is mechanically computable and never a per-nation judgement call. A node whose effects include MilitaryEfficiency, MilitaryStrength, DiffusionEmission or CostReduction is SOVEREIGNTY-SIDE: holding it means this nation could PRODUCE it, so operating an imported article does not qualify. Every other node is USE-SIDE: deployed and in operational use here is enough, whoever built it, because the effect such a node pays is a productivity, health or output effect and that effect is real in the country where the machine runs. Of the 48 technologies the tree lets anyone hold in 1990, 17 are sovereignty-side and 31 are use-side.

DATA-KEYED TAIL NATION. This nation is outside the 29 authored majors, so nothing here was authored technology by technology: a grant is made only where one of two named published global series supports it, and nothing is modelled, estimated or interpolated. A short list, or an empty one, is the correct outcome of that rule and not a gap in the work.

Data-keyed tail nation: not one of the 29 authored majors. Only the two series named in ruling 3 were consulted - WHO/UNICEF WUENIC DTP3 1990 and World Bank IT.CEL.SETS. Nothing was modelled, estimated or interpolated, and no other evidence was admitted. ISO3 key used for both series: MYS.
WUENIC DTP3 1990 = 90% against the 80% UCI-1990 threshold: bio_universal_immunisation GRANTED.
IT.CEL.SETS at 31 December 1989 = 39419 against a threshold of any positive count: comm_cellular_analogue GRANTED.

The other 46 grantable 1990 technologies are BLANK for this nation by design, not by oversight: the 17 sovereignty-side entries are unreachable by any use-in-operation series, and no published global series was named that keys the remaining 29 use-side entries.

granted.source: World Bank WDI IT.CEL.SETS 'Mobile cellular subscriptions', retrieved from the World Bank indicator API (api.worldbank.org/v2), source id 2, lastupdated 2026-07-13. Series values: MYS, 1989 = 39419 subscriptions and 1990 = 86620 subscriptions. The series is a YEAR-END STOCK, so the 1989 figure describes 31 December 1989, i.e. the game's start instant of 1 January 1990: a network was carrying paying subscribers before the start date. All cellular in service at that date was analogue (NMT, AMPS, TACS, C-Netz, RTMS); GSM had no commercial service anywhere until mid-1991.

WHO/UNICEF WUENIC DTP3 immunisation coverage (% of surviving infants), retrieved from the UNICEF public SDMX API, dataflow UNICEF:IMMUNISATION(1.0), indicator IM_DTP3, DATA_SOURCE field 'WHO/UNICEF estimates of national immunization coverage, 2025 revision'. Series value: MYS, 1990 = 90%, at or above the 80% WHO/UNICEF Universal Childhood Immunization (UCI-1990) target that defines this technology's name.
